metadata.description: Single source of truth for Balder publication figure colors. Read by Python (code/tools/figure_style.py). Colorblind-safe, print-safe. Reserved-axis contract (v1.1): recurring cross-figure encodings get locked colors that never collide WITHIN a figure -- model (RF=blue / LR=vermillion), actionability/up=purple, down=teal, feature category (demographic=teal / sample-type=purple / technical=gray), hit literature status (previously reported=orange / unresolved=muted gray, drawn as an OUTLINE so it survives mono print; v1.3, 2026-10-23: the former 'novel' state was withdrawn with the gene-level novelty claims, workstream S1). Within-figure-only encodings (cancer_systems, institutions, categorical_values) draw from the qualitative ramp with no global meaning. v1.2 (2026-09-12) adds the `neutrals` ramp -- the unencoded vocabulary (ink / annotation / rule / grid / band / ...) that every panel needs and that scripts previously invented per-file -- plus `graphviz_theme` so the STROBE diagram is themed from here too. NOTHING in a panel script may hard-code a color: reach for a `neutrals` key rather than inventing a gray. See figures/style/FIGURE_STYLE_GUIDE.md.

neutrals_usage.ink: Marker edge strokes, axis spines, a hard zero/unity reference line.
neutrals_usage.annotation: Secondary text drawn inside the plot area (n = labels, value callouts).
neutrals_usage.rule: Structural divider lines and dashed threshold/reference rules (q = 0.05, cohort mean). Replaces the ad-hoc 'red' reference lines -- a reference mark is scaffolding, not a data series, so it must not spend a hue.
neutrals_usage.muted: A de-emphasised or 'other'/unclassified series. Same hex as `neutral` and as feature_groups.technical -- only use it as a data color where technical-vs-other cannot be confused.
neutrals_usage.inactive: Tested-but-not-significant marks. Deliberately lighter than `muted` so it reads as a separate class beside grey data points (Fig 4C).
neutrals_usage.on_fill: Text or edges drawn on top of a saturated fill.
